[FACT] User has a growing collection of vintage cameras.

[FACT] User currently has 17 vintage cameras, including a Brownie Hawkeye.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended a dedicated space with a consistent temperature (around 65°F to 70°F) and humidity level (around 50%) for storing cameras.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested using camera cases or high-quality, acid-free boxes for storage to protect cameras from dust, scratches, and impact.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised using soft, padded dividers to separate cameras and prevent scratches or damage.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended avoiding stacking cameras to prevent pressure on lenses and mechanisms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested using silica gel packets or a dehumidifier to maintain stable humidity levels.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised against extreme temperatures and direct sunlight to prevent material degradation and fading.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended handling cameras with clean, dry hands or gloves to prevent oil damage.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested using a soft, dry brush or blower bulb to gently remove dust from cameras.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised using a soft, microfiber cloth and gentle cleaning solution for cleaning lenses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended lubricating moving parts with light machine oil or silicone lubricant.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested checking and replacing seals to prevent light leaks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended documenting the collection, including history, condition, and maintenance performed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested storing accessories separately in labeled containers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended considering climate-controlled storage if living in extreme climate conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested joining a camera collector community for shared knowledge and resources.
